$comment: AMAZWI — the visual identity for HARRY. Single source of truth. Every surface (projector HUD, phone PWA, build console, CLI banner) derives from this file. Do not hard-code hex values or font names anywhere else in the repo.

colorSemantics.$comment: Colour carries meaning in Amazwi. These rules are not decorative — they are how the user reads system state from across a room.
colorSemantics.lime: Local. Alive. Nothing has left this machine.
colorSemantics.pale: Attention, or data in flight to a cloud bridge. Pale means either 'I need you' or 'this left the laptop'.
colorSemantics.faint: Dormant or failed. The absence of lime is the alarm.
colorSemantics.rule: Never introduce a third hue (no red, amber or blue) for state. Meaning is carried by lime / pale / faint plus motion.

display.use: Headings, the HARRY wordmark, state titles on the projector.

mono.use: Labels, skill names, commands, telemetry, everything with a letter-spaced uppercase treatment.

motion.reducedMotion: Respect prefers-reduced-motion everywhere. When reduced, the waveform holds a static profile and state is carried by colour and label only.

waveform.$comment: The signature element. Seven bars form the letter H: two tall uprights each side, a short crossbar in the middle. The H MUST remain legible at every amplitude — this is why inner bars are capped below the outer bars.

smoothing.$comment: Rise fast so speech feels responsive, fall slow so it never strobes.

states.$comment: Labels match the projector strings in roadmap Phase 12 exactly. priority: higher wins when two states race — approval always beats everything.

idle.label: STANDING BY
idle.meaning: Harry is up and listening for the wake word. Nothing is running.

listening.label: LISTENING
listening.meaning: Mic is open. Bars track your actual voice level.

thinking.label: THINKING LOCALLY
thinking.meaning: A local Ollama model is reasoning. Nothing has left the machine.

bridging.label: USING {agent}
bridging.meaning: A cloud bridge (Codex CLI or Claude Code) is working. Pale is deliberate: it tells you data left the laptop.

working.label: RUNNING {task}
working.meaning: A deterministic skill is executing — tests, git, files. Not model reasoning.

speaking.label: SPEAKING
speaking.meaning: Kokoro is talking. Bars track the TTS output.

approval.label: APPROVAL REQUIRED
approval.meaning: Harry is blocked on you. Bars freeze tall and blink slowly. This must be unmissable from three metres.

done.label: TASK COMPLETE
done.meaning: Transient. Flashes bright, settles, auto-returns to idle.

error.label: FAILED
error.meaning: Something broke. Bars collapse to a dim flat line — in a system where lime means alive, its absence is the alarm.

rules: State must be readable without reading text — colour and motion carry it first, the label confirms.
One idea on screen at a time. Never a dashboard.
No scroll, no hover, no small text. Nothing interactive.
Dark by default; the room is dim and the projector is the only light source.
Thumb-first: primary actions in the lower third.
The waveform shrinks to a status strip, it does not dominate the screen.
Approval cards are the most important surface in the whole app — they must be reachable in one tap from anywhere.
Works offline; assume the tailnet drops.
Long-form and scroll-driven. This is the only surface where parallax and prose belong.
